claim: A 5-sigma cardiac magnetocardiography (MCG) signal from a human subject at 10m range through a 1-5m rock/concrete wall is detectable using a gradiometric pair of commercially-available OPM sensors (QuSpin QZFM Gen-3, 10 fT/sqrt(Hz)) with ambient magnetic noise rejection, given integration time of 60-300 seconds in a magnetically quiet environment (ambient noise < 50 fT/sqrt(Hz)).
confidence_rationale: Low confidence because: (1) the physics is sound — MCG at 10m is ~50 fT (dipole r^-3 scaling from 50 pT at 1m), which is at the QuSpin noise floor — but the signal-to-noise calculation assumes an implausibly quiet ambient environment; (2) the gradiometric rejection ratio required (~10^3-10^4) to subtract ambient field fluctuations in a non-shielded or portable setup has not been demonstrated at these signal levels in field conditions; (3) wall conductivity and permeability could reduce the already-marginal signal further. Single source chain (HW-2026-036 + dipole physics). The physics is clean but the environmental assumptions are fragile.
test_design: 1. Obtain two QuSpin QZFM Gen-3 OPM sensors ($20k each, commercially available). Configure as a first-order gradiometer with 0.5m baseline. 2. Establish magnetically quiet indoor environment (existing concrete building, away from HVAC/elevators). Measure ambient magnetic noise floor with no subject present. Target: < 50 fT/sqrt(Hz) after gradiometric subtraction. 3. Subject (70 kg adult) stands on opposite side of concrete wall (1-2m thickness) at measured distance 10m from sensor pair. Run 300 seconds of MCG recording. 4. Apply matched-filter at cardiac frequency (0.5-2 Hz fundamental, up to 5th harmonic). Compute SNR of R-wave peak in frequency domain. 5. Increase subject distance from 5m to 30m in 5m steps, recording 300s at each distance. Fit SNR ~ r^-3 power law. Report minimum detectable distance at 5-sigma threshold with 300s integration. Refutation criterion: If SNR < 2 at 10m with 300s integration in quiet indoor environment, the ambient noise floor is the limiting factor, not fundamental physics.
refutation_criteria: Hypothesis is refuted if: (a) measured ambient noise floor exceeds 500 fT/sqrt(Hz) after gradiometric subtraction (rendering the signal undetectable at any integration time), OR (b) SNR at 10m with 300s integration is < 2 sigma even in a dedicated magnetically-shielded room, OR (c) the r^-3 power law fit yields alpha significantly different from 3.0 (indicating the wall or sensor geometry introduces geometric corrections that kill the signal faster than expected).
hardware_required: Two QuSpin QZFM Gen-3 OPM units (~$40k total), data acquisition system (NI DAQ or similar, ~$5k), magnetically quiet room or access to a hospital biomagnetic lab for shielded room comparison. No cryogenics, no lasers beyond what is built into OPM units. Total estimated budget: $50k (at upper end of independent-researcher budget).

feasibility_notes.hardware: QuSpin QZFM Gen-3 OPM: commercially available, ~$20k per unit. Two units for gradiometer = $40k. Within $50k independent-researcher budget. No cryogenics. Ships in 8-12 weeks. Data acquisition: NI USB-6356 DAQ ~$3k.
feasibility_notes.physics: MCG signal at 10m: 50 pT * (1m/10m)^3 = 50 fT. QuSpin noise floor: 10 fT/sqrt(Hz). In 300s integration, effective noise = 10/sqrt(300) = 0.58 fT — theoretical SNR ~86. HOWEVER: unshielded ambient lab noise is 100-100,000 fT/sqrt(Hz). Gradiometric pair with 0.5m baseline suppresses spatially correlated noise by ~50-100x (ratio of baseline to noise correlation length). This may be sufficient in a quiet building (power-off industrial space) but not in a typical university lab near elevators/HVAC. Shielded room access (hospital MEG lab) would guarantee success and is available via academic collaboration at zero marginal cost.
feasibility_notes.math: No no-go theorems. Dipole field physics is textbook. Gradiometric rejection ratio is the engineering unknown.
feasibility_notes.resource: Total budget: $43k (two OPMs + DAQ + misc). Marginal cost for shielded-room comparison: $0 (academic collaboration). Time to first result: 3-6 months post-procurement.

deep_research_clarification_2026_06_27: DEEPRESEARCH-rydberg-rf-2026-05-18.md §9.2 confirmed that Rydberg augmentation of this hypothesis is not viable: Rydberg E-field sensors are 3-5 orders of magnitude short of MCG signals at the relevant DC-1 kHz band, the signal is magnetic not electric, and Rydberg magnetometry is not within reach of the MCG floor. This hypothesis was always OPM-only; the clarification simply pre-rejects any future 'add Rydberg' variant. The OPM-only path remains TESTABLE_NOW but inherits the original confidence_rationale: ambient noise floor (not sensor sensitivity) is the binding constraint, and shielded-room access (hospital MEG lab, academic collaboration, ~$0 marginal cost) is essentially required to clear the refutation_criteria threshold. Recommend: do not pursue the $43k unshielded build; pursue the shielded-room collaboration first as a zero-cost feasibility test before any hardware procurement.

pipeline_provenance.conjecture_stage: Generated from adjudicated through-rock physics (HW-2026-036 OPM sensitivity analysis): at 10m, MCG signal ~50 fT is at the QuSpin QZFM noise floor, meaning detection is physically marginal but not fundamentally impossible. Tier 1 confirmed: (1) skin depth at 10 Hz in rock ~5000m so ULF penetrates freely, (2) MCG dipole falls as r^-3, (3) mountain-scale claims (100m+) are definitively refuted. The 1-30m range is the frontier. A successful demonstration at 10m through concrete would be a novel result (MEG labs measure MCG at <1m; through-wall biomagnetic sensing at meter-scale is not yet demonstrated in peer-reviewed literature). The gradiometric noise rejection is the critical experimental challenge, not the fundamental physics.
